story_candidates.title: Two more studies of agent-written code: size and review, not the agent

ai_path.connection: Direct: research on code written by AI coding agents.

story_candidates.angle: Two arXiv papers: after change size is taken into account, code-quality differences between coding agents mostly disappear in one, and in the other reviewer engagement is the strongest signal that an agent's change is merged.
story_candidates.note: For journalist-ai, categories AI. Ready. A follow-up article (standing answer 100): S83 (five-coding-agents-reverts-security-waits) carries its update of 24 November, so new material becomes a follow-up article; link S83 and repeat none of its content. Two arXiv papers read by the researcher, both the papers' own figures and unchecked. (1) A paper on merged agent-written bug-fix pull requests (arXiv 2601.20109, its PDF read in part; the page header names the MSR 2026 conference, 13 to 14 April 2026): 8,106 fix pull requests narrowed to 1,210 merged ones in Python repositories (206 projects), SonarQube run before and after each merge; after normalising issues by lines of code modified, median issue density is broadly similar across most agents with no statistically significant difference, one agent (Cursor) a partial exception with a higher median; the paper says per-agent differences are largely driven by change volume; its limits: Python only, no matched human baseline, static post-merge signals only, very imbalanced agent counts (agent-level results exploratory), tool severity labels may not reflect production risk. (2) A paper on review and integration (arXiv 2602.19441, abstract page only, submitted 23 February 2026, accepted at MSR 2026): reviewer engagement has the strongest correlation with a pull request being merged; larger changes and force pushes are associated with a lower likelihood of merging; the abstract says integration depends not only on code quality but on alignment with review and coordination practices. Say plainly what each measures (issues flagged by a code-analysis tool; whether a pull request was merged), that the second paper was read from its abstract only, that neither measures production incidents, and that the studies use different data and questions so they are not a single ranking; no verdict on AI code and no vendor ranking. Explain 'issue density', 'pull request' and 'force push' in plain words at first use. 300 to 700 words.

for_the_fact_checker.what: Papers' figures only: the first read in part (PDF), the second from its abstract; neither measures production incidents; the first has no human baseline and is Python-only; the studies use different questions and data.
